items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Sol coached Steve Allen on synchronizing the camera shots with the sound track.

ctx.x: We were talking about when you went out to California to do the picture, The Benny Goodman Story. Now there should be some interesting things to tell about that. Let's see, Sol Yaged was teaching somebody to play Benny ...

That's right, Steve Allen played the role of Benny Goodman, and Sol coached Steve Allen on synchronizing the camera shots with the sound track. See, they recorded the whole sound track -- the music was all recorded first, and then the camera work was done later with the sound track being blasted over loud speakers for the musicians to hear and memorize the improvisations as they go over it again and again, until they finally got a pretty good synchronization of sound and sight.

So it was recorded first, because Goodman recorded all the clarinet on the sound track, but Steve Allen was photographed doing it all, and Sol was his coach and taught him how to hold the clarinet and to make it appear plausible that he was actually playing the clarinet when he wasn't.

items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: I used to go over there with Buck Clayton, with Urbie Green, Zoot Simms, Teddy Wilson went out there. We all went out there to sit in and play every night.

ctx.x: You and your wife handled all your affairs for all those years.

Everything. She took care of everything. When we had to make the contract deal to go to Hollywood to make the movie she handled the business for me. We went out there for three months and we had a glorious time, glorious time. We used to go playing at night, Monk, we went to a jam session place every night in Glendale, California. I remember it as if it was yesterday. It was called The Melody Club. I used to go over there with Buck Clayton, with Urbie Green, Zoot Simms, Teddy Wilson went out there. We all went…
Yeah, so it was like, everybody was what they call lip syncing I guess, right?
